name: DOM element serialization (minify / to_string / prettify)
description:
HARNESS RULES FOR THIS GROUP: (a) the MAIN PATH below runs on every input with the full input, exactly as listed; it is the baseline, the rest of this Logic Group only adds to it. (b) Entries marked 'same core / alternative' reach the same internal code as the main call: never replace the main call with them and never run all of them on every input (fan-out kills exec/s); if used, run at most one of them as an extra step chosen by spare input bits. (c) A configuration switch must never take inputs away from the main path; options that only add code (e.g. detail/verbose output) stay ON. (d) This list is incomplete; what the project's own fuzzers, tests and examples do with the target stays in scope. (e) Nothing the fuzz input can make slow or hang may run on every input: no allocation sized from an untrusted header field, no call with a known library hang (listed below), no callback/selector that aborts the main call for a large share of inputs; the bytes handed to the parser start at a fixed offset (offset 0 when the format has a magic number), so the fuzzer can find magic numbers and header fields.
MAIN PATH (keep on every input; verified in simdjson (qf-work/src/simdjson-c2) source):
1. Split the input with the project helper FuzzData(Data, Size).splitIntoStrings() (fuzz/FuzzUtils.h:26-42, 117-126: separator "\n~~\n"); strings[0] is the JSON document (the whole input when there is no separator), strings[1] a JSON pointer, strings[2] a JSONPath (empty if missing). No mode/selector bytes in front of the JSON.
2. simdjson::dom::parser parser; dom::element doc; if (parser.parse(strings[0]).get(doc)) return 0; (include/simdjson/dom/parser.h:237).
3. std::string s1 = simdjson::minify(doc) (include/simdjson/dom/serialization.h:274) on EVERY parsed input.
4. Structural navigation, every input: if doc.get_array() succeeds, minify(arr) and minify(child) for up to 16 children; if doc.get_object() succeeds, minify(obj) and minify(field.value) for up to 16 fields (element-inl.h:317, 326; array-inl.h / object-inl.h iterators).
5. Input-selected navigation, every input: doc.at_pointer(strings[1]) → minify(leaf); if strings[2] exists, doc.at_path(strings[2]) → minify(leaf) (element-inl.h:427, 461; at_path converts JSONPath via json_path_to_pointer_conversion in include/simdjson/jsonpathutil.h:58). This is where element-inl/object-inl/array-inl/jsonpathutil coverage comes from (about 280 lines the previous LG harness never reached).
6. Round trip: a second dom::parser parses s1 and minify() runs again (tests/minify_tests.cpp:50-62 idempotency check); also the simdjson_result<T> overload minify(parser2.parse(s1)) inside try/catch when SIMDJSON_EXCEPTIONS (serialization.h:277).
Never call parser.parse_many(...) / document_stream in this harness: with a batch_size smaller than the input, document_stream::start()/next() loops forever (include/simdjson/dom/document_stream-inl.h:192-202, 254-255, the batch start does not advance when stage 1 returns EMPTY; also seen with the json_sequence stream_format). This is a library hang, not a harness misuse: the previous LG harness hit 67 x 25 s timeouts, about 28 of the 30 minutes.
ADDITIONS on top (spare input bits only): at most one extra per input chosen by spare bits: prettify(doc) or to_string(doc) (same core / alternative: same string_builder walk with pretty_formatter / identical to minify, serialization.h:274-311); or the raw-buffer simdjson::minify(buf, len, dst, dst_len) (include/simdjson/minify.h:26, stage-1 json_minifier) with a destination of at least len bytes.

FEATURE DESCRIPTION (from the Logic Group stage):
simdjson::minify<T>(x) (and its sibling simdjson::to_string<T>/prettify<T>) walk a parsed DOM document's tape representation and re-serialize it into a JSON string using the internal::string_builder<formatter> template. Because the tape is produced by parsing untrusted JSON bytes (dom::parser::parse/parse_many/load), bugs in the tape-walking state machine (depth tracking, recursion at MAX_DEPTH, number formatting, string escaping, NaN/Infinity handling) or in the string_view decoding of tape-embedded keys/strings are directly reachable from attacker-controlled JSON text, making this an important round-trip (parse -> serialize) fuzzing target. There is also a separate, lower-level "raw minify" path (simdjson::minify(const char*, len, dst, dst_len) dispatching to implementation::minify) that minifies JSON bytes directly without building a DOM tape at all, exercising a different (SIMD-based) state machine for stripping whitespace while respecting string/escape boundaries.
- simdjson::minify<T>: target; calls to_string<T> -> internal::string_builder<mini_formatter>::append(element/array/object/key_value_pair), the core tape-walking minifier.
- simdjson::to_string<T>: variant, identical tape walk but exposed as the "canonical" string conversion; shares the same core.
- simdjson::prettify<T>: variant, same tape walk via internal::string_builder<pretty_formatter>, adding indentation/newline formatting branches (print_newline/print_indents/print_space) not exercised by minify.
- simdjson::dom::parser::parse (and parse_into_document / load / parse_many): source — builds the dom::element/dom::document (and its internal tape) from raw JSON bytes that minify/to_string/prettify will walk; without it the tape has no attacker-controlled content.
- simdjson::dom::parser::parse_many: source/variant — produces a document_stream of multiple documents (NDJSON), each separately fed into minify, exercising the tape walker repeatedly with different structures per fuzz run.
- simdjson::minify(const char*, size_t, char*, size_t&) (free function over raw buffers, dispatching to implementation::minify): variant — an alternate minification path that works directly on raw JSON bytes via the active SIMD implementation's stage-1 structural scan, instead of on a parsed DOM tape; useful to cross-check behavior/differential-test against the DOM-based minify.
The input space is entirely the JSON document(s) fed to parser::parse/parse_many: object vs array vs scalar roots, nesting depth (branches at MAX_DEPTH=16 in string_builder::append trigger a different recursive code path), string content requiring escaping (quotes, backslashes, control chars 0x00-0x1F mapped through the `escaped` table), big integers stored as BIGINT tape entries printed raw, INT64/UINT64/DOUBLE number formatting (including NaN/Infinity/-Infinity when SIMDJSON_ENABLE_NAN_INF is set), empty arrays/objects ([] / {}), and for parse_many additionally the batch_size and stream_format (ndjson vs json) parameters that change how input bytes are split into separate documents before each is minified.
